SGP.note: Read off the create screen for each of the three work types on 1 September 2026. Twenty-eight fields across the space. Eighteen of them appear on all three types; the other ten appear on some and not others, and where that matters it is called out.
groups: Fixed when the ticket is created.
Epic, Task or Sub-task. Nothing here is created automatically, so whoever opens the ticket picks it.
The one-line title. In SGP this is doing a lot of work, because there is no other field that says what the ticket is.

Content, Business, Product, QA, Innovation, Marketing or Community. Required on the Epic and the Task, and it defaults to Business Team, so check it. The Sub-task form does not ask for it, yet every Sub-task has a value, so something else is filling it in.
One person. The one to change if the ticket is stuck.
A fixed list of named people rather than a user picker, so it has to be edited in Jira settings when the team changes.
The detail. Optional on every type, and often empty.
Worker side (App), Company side (Web), Moodle, Plugin, Data, Environment, Course Content. On the Epic and the Task only.
Mobile App, or Web (Moodle, Custom Plugins or Blocks).
Free text. On the Task only.
Where it sits in the tree
The ticket above this one. Required on the Sub-task, optional on the Task. That is why 5,960 of the 9,107 Tasks in SGP sit under no Epic at all.
The older way of pointing at an Epic, superseded by Parent but still on the form for the Task and the Sub-task.
A short name for the Epic, separate from its Summary. On the Epic only.
Only when someone links two tickets by hand. On the Sub-task only.
Jira's own components list, which is empty for this project. On the Sub-task only.
Empty for this project. On the Sub-task only.
Jira's sprint field. It is on the Sub-task form only, and nothing in the space sets it.
A second date field alongside Due date. Two fields for the same idea.
Critical, High, Medium, Low, Lowest. Defaults to Low, so a Low priority usually means nobody set one.
All users, or Managers - Content team. The second one hides the ticket from everyone outside that group.

CIP.note: Read off the create screen for each of the three work types on 1 September 2026. The Epic carries 24 fields and the Task 25. The Sub-task carries 17 of them, and only Parent, Project and Summary are required on it.
groups: Fixed when the ticket is created.
What kind of idea it is
MVP, Feedback Action Items, or Process Improvements. Required on the Epic and the Task. Thirty-three tickets were created before it became required and still have nothing in it.
Learner, Compliance, Brand, or Software Changes. Who or what gets better if this is done.
Where the suggestion arrived from. The form pre-fills the prompt "NPS/Stakeholder Feedback/Survey/Other - Specify Others" as a reminder of the options. Required on the Task, optional on the Epic.
The person whose input this is. Required on the Task, optional on the Epic.
A link to the survey, the ticket or the recording the idea came from.
Which course or asset the idea is about.
What is being done about it
The plan. Required on the Task, optional on the Epic.
What was actually done. Filled in later.

What stakeholders said when the small version was shown to them. There are two separate fields with this name, one on the Epic and a different one on the Task, so a search for one will not find the other.
The ticket above this one. Required on the Sub-task.
Only when someone links two tickets by hand.
When the idea is meant to be finished.
When the small version went out. Only meaningful once the idea reaches Ready.
Jira's own due date, alongside Target End Date. Two fields for the same idea.
Where the ticket sits in a board's order.
Filled in by Jira if code is linked. Nothing links code to CIP.
Filled in by Jira if a design tool is linked. Nothing is linked.
